prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve.
Asset type: refined side-view Fire-school shield-catch animation sheet, not a concept comparison.
Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET: the user's selected Shield Catch six-pose sheet. Refine ONLY this selected motion, preserve the same Laema design, sword, small round navy shield, outfit, material shading and right-facing viewpoint.
Deliver EXACTLY EIGHT successive full-body poses in a FOUR-COLUMNS by TWO-ROWS equal-cell grid. Transparent background, no painted backdrop, no text, numbers, borders, floor, shadows, opponent or other props. Landscape sheet about 2048x1024, eight 512-square cells. Each figure inside its own cell with ample clear margins. Top row 1-4, bottom row 5-8.
Character invariants: adult woman, long silver-white ponytail tied in red, cream rolled sleeves, short blue vest, red waist sash, brown trousers, boots and gloves. Right hand grips one PLAIN STRAIGHT SILVER SWORD with consistent simple crossguard and blade length; left forearm/hand carries one small circular NAVY SHIELD with silver rim and central steel boss. Preserve the selected rendered-volume sprite appearance, not anime, chibi or clean-vector art. Crisp readable small-scale materials; no redesign, armor or extra weapons.
Motion refinement: COMPACT SHIELD CATCH, not a shield bash. Keep boots planted at EXACT same cell coordinates and same spread in all eight poses. Same body height, hip position, camera and lighting. Only small upper-body compression and left-arm shield rotation. Right sword hand stays near the right hip, blade extends forward-right about 15-25 degrees above horizontal throughout; the sword NEVER swings or changes hand. Shield rises smoothly to cover upper chest and cheek, left elbow stays close, then a tiny outward wrist tilt catches and sheds contact; shield never lunges toward an opponent.
Eight poses:
1. Comfortable ready, shield at chest, sword quiet above belt.
2. Close the left elbow and begin raising shield, only slight shoulder compression.
3. Intermediate shield raise, edge moves toward cheek, head stays visible.
4. Intercept guard, shield covers upper chest and part of cheek, feet remain fixed.
5. Catch/contact: slight upper-body compression (no more than 2 percent body height), shield wrist tilts a LITTLE outward. ONE tiny orange spark on upper OUTER shield rim only. No explosion or magic wall.
6. Release the compression, shield rotates back halfway, no spark.
7. Lower the shield smoothly toward chest and restore ready shoulders.
8. Same ready stance as pose1, identical lower-body silhouette and sword angle.
Draw coherent in-between poses instead of unrelated illustrations. Keep shield diameter, shield face perspective, sword proportions, face, ponytail volume and red sash consistent. Never grow the shield to cover the entire face. No advancing, jumping, turning away, deep crouch, counterstrike, exaggerated recoil, blade trails, hammer, staff or blue magic. Every full figure and sword tip completely within its cell. Actual alpha transparency.
